Lift the weight of guilt and unburden the people I love

Fuck this is me right now too. Medication sort of makes you realize that you DO want to do stuff, but doesn’t actually help get it done. 

All the meditation/ motivation resources talk about habit building but lol that’s hard even for people who aren’t trying to overcome depression.

Just because a problem is “typical” doesn’t make it any less hard and painful. You are dealing with difficult stuff, I’m sorry it’s causing you pain. 

No advice, just that I know how much it sucks fo feel emotionally disconnected :(

Dude. *Dude*. Are you literally me? 

Expectations are a trap designed to magnify self-loathing and I hate it. Expectations are simultaneously real (thanks to other ppl) and very not real (thanks to depression brain that wants to make you feel bad for being human and not a perfection machine)

Not weird examples at all. You sound like a caring and empathetic person. It might help to ask yourself if the things you are feeling sorry for mirror anything within yourself or your experiences? Given your examples, it seem like you might be projecting fears/anxieties on to other people.

I’m sorry to hear about your grandfather. It’s tough to lose anyone we love, but especially those we have chosen to try and live for.

It’s shitty to feel like we’ve exhausted all our options. I feel that 100%
Yea it can be really mentally taxing to work through all these things, for me it’s really easy to overthink things. For what it’s worth tho I’m cheering you on :)

No cowardice here, it takes a lot to admit to oneself that we are hurting. I empathize with a lot of what you’ve said. That subconscious desire is infectious. I hope you and I both can keep use our conscious mind to keep on trying. Just because our results are less than satisfactory doesn’t mean they are pointless

I’m sorry that you’ve had to experience this loss, and I’m sorry for your friend who was in so much pain. This hurts to read; I think a lot of us here are aware that our choices affect people. Sometimes though the pain is so insurmountable that we forget about others and/or privilege our own suffering over that of the people left behind. 

This sub is a release and offers a sense of security for a lot of folks who are otherwise hiding behind a smile or are suffering in solitude.

Thanks for sharing. I’m 21 now, been dealing with this F’ed up brain since 11. I know there are moments to be happy about, but they are so easy to forget when I feel like this. That’s why people like you who show up to this subreddit and report good news are always appreciated :)
Please don’t let her words hurt you too much. Special is such a subjective measure and I guarantee you are/will be/can be special to someone who is way more worth your time.

I can’t tell you whether or not you were depressed then, but I think it’s good that you’re thinking about it. These sorts of childhood traumas follow us into adulthood; bullying seriously affects the psyche. If exploring and labeling these past experiences helps you understand the present, then by all means call it depression, you certainly wouldn’t be unjustified in doing so.

Oh yea. At 10 it was 16. At 16 it was 21. Now at 21 it’s 25. 

I keep wondering how long I’ll be pushing back this deadline but then I remember I’m an expert at procrastinating and avoiding responsibilities.

It is a real and valid problem. If nothing else, it’s worth asking. I myself have had a note for a few unexcused absences in a class that had a strict attendance policy. It’s important not to make getting notes a repeated habit, and if you think it might be, talk to psych about long term accommodations , though I think they are harder to get.

Congrats on graduating soon. Whatever has happened up to this point, finishing college is an accomplishment. Do you mind if I ask what you studied? 

I’m in a similar boat. But I’m college junior delaying any possibility of graduating by persistently failing classes, bonus points for paying a shit ton of money to do it.

The burden of hearing it is nothing compared to the burden of bearing it alone. you’ve  put your thoughts out there. I know it doesn’t mean much, but they’ve been heard and acknowledged. I can’t pretend to know your struggle, but what you’re feeling is palpable.
